name: MikroTik RouterOS
author: Netlens
description: Reads a MikroTik router, switch or access point (RouterOS 7.1+): the device as a network node, MikroTik neighbours (MNDP/LLDP) as child nodes, and the devices it knows as clients with their bridge port, DHCP lease, ARP entry or Wi-Fi registration (band, signal, link speed). Netlens uses this to place devices in the hierarchy and to show Wi-Fi signal history. Read-only: only GET requests to the REST API.

info.title: Set up the router (once)
info.text: RouterOS 7.1+ has a REST API on its web service (www on port 80 or www-ssl on 443). Create a user in a group that can only read, enable the service, and limit it to the machine that runs Netlens. Paste these lines into the router's terminal (change the password and the address).
info.code:
/user group add name=netlens-ro policy=read,api,rest-api,test,!local,!telnet,!ssh,!ftp,!reboot,!write,!policy,!winbox,!password,!web,!sniff,!sensitive,!romon
/user add name=netlens group=netlens-ro password=CHANGE-ME address=192.168.0.10
/ip service enable www-ssl
/ip service set www-ssl address=192.168.0.10/32
# plain http instead of https: /ip service enable www  (the password then travels unencrypted)

config.label: MikroTik devices
config.help: One line per RouterOS device. List the router and every MikroTik switch or access point; give each switch or access point the address of the device it is plugged into under 'Uplink' if the neighbour list does not already show it.

columns.label: Role
columns.placeholder: auto, gateway, switch, ap or node
columns.help: auto: a device that does NAT (masquerade) is the gateway, any other is a switch.

config.label: Verify TLS certificate
config.help: Only for https addresses. RouterOS uses a self-signed certificate unless you installed your own.
